 11:53 pm, November 14, 2026 Rounding up some afternoon scores
 How is it already time for some night games? 
 Week 11 has flown by with excitement happening all across the afternoon slate. Let's dive into some final score:
 No. 9 Indiana 27, No. 18 Southern Cal 13 
 Despite a healthy Josh Hoover, Indiana went with Grant Wilson -- and boy, are they glad they did.
 The Hoosiers snuck past the Trojans 27-13 anchored by Wilson's solid stat line: 17-of-27 for 305 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. 
 Charlie Becker DIVES into the end zone to extend the @IndianaFootball lead 💥 Watch on CBS https://t.co/7esRSzECIR
— Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) November 14, 2026 
 No. 1 Georgia 48, No. 22 Missouri 21 
 The Bulldogs, who opened the game with an interception, dominated the Tigers 48-21 in Athens. Backed by a Nate Fraizer hat trick, Georgia will advance to 9-1. 
 No. 16 Oregon 31, Michigan 7 
 Dylan Raiola had himself a game, going 20-of-28 and racking up 341 yards for four touchdowns. 
 On the other hand, Michigan's quarterback room, not so much.
 Tommy Carr, who started 1-of-5 for 8 yards, was replaced by Bryce Underwood early. Underwood, however, wasn't quite what the Wolverines were looking for in a backup, finishing 2-of-8 for 26 yards. Neither signal caller had a touchdown.  
 All kinds of room for Dakorien! @RaiolaDylan 🤝 @thereal_kori2x #GoDucks https://t.co/Qh9vDMEkBe
— Oregon Football (@oregonfootball) November 14, 2026 
 No. 5 Notre Dame 41, Boston College 7 
 The Fighting Irish certainly didn't struggle against Boston College, walking away with a 41-7 win over the Eagles.
 Notre Dame running back Jonaz Walton recorded 141 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries.

 share with Facebook copy link 9:31 pm, November 14, 2026 Some SEC shenanigans
 If there's anything this college football season has taught us, it’s that the unexpected should be expected — especially within the Top 25 and amongst SEC teams.
 No. 8 Tennessee is trailing an unranked Texas A&M team 6-7 heading into the half. If the Volunteers lose, they’ll be bunched within the three-loss team category of teams that could make the committee’s final bracket.
 Meanwhile, in Athens, No. 1 Georgia is routing No. 22 Missouri 21-0 — and the second quarter just started. The Tigers opened things up with an interception, setting up Nate Fraizer for an early score. Fraizer has two touchdowns on nine carries for just over 40 yards.

 Tonight, keep an eye on No. 6 Texas at No. 21 LSU and No. 11 Kentucky versus Florida . Truthfully, nobody really knows how these games could go.
 share with Facebook copy link 8:54 pm, November 14, 2026 Ferris State breaks NCAA DII football record with 41st consecutive win
 It’s been 805 days since Ferris State last lost a game. That means the DII win record is now the Bulldogs'.
 Ferris State routed Roosevelt 63-20 on Saturday , its 41st consecutive win that sets a DII football record. The Bulldogs led 42-0 and piled up 590 yards, with Marcel Jones running for three of Ferris State's seven rushing touchdowns.
 The Bulldogs haven't lost since Aug. 31, 2024. The streak has included nine consecutive wins in the playoff and two national titles. The program also has won the DII national title four times in the last five seasons.
 It's not the only long streak, either. Ferris State's 35 consecutive home wins at Top Taggart Field is also a DII record.
 Jake Price punches in HIS first of the day! Ferris State goes up 56-14 with a 4-yard rush by Jake Price💨 📺: https://t.co/YOfsnNXgLj @GLIAC | @FerrisFootball #GLIAC | Aug 27 - Nov 14 | Live on FloCollege https://t.co/iNE9Om3UMT
— FloCollege | Football (@FloCollegeFB) November 14, 2026 
 The record-breaking win is just the latest blowout win for the Bulldogs. Last week, Fresno State  tied Grand Valley State’s 40-game DII win streak (set 2005-07)  after an 80-0 win over Wayne State (MI).

 share with Facebook copy link 8:32 pm, November 14, 2026 An afternoon scores update
 The noon slate is coming to a close, so let’s catch up on today’s action so far.
 No. 20 Ohio State survived Northwestern 28-19 despite the Wildcats’ last second six-play, 67-yard touchdown drive as the clock hit zero.
 No. 7 Miami outlasted Duke, coming up with a 36-25 victory. Darian Mensah went 30-of-41 for 382 yards and one touchdown.
 Tied 20-20 with two minutes to go, Maryland and Wisconsin nearly found themselves in overtime, but the Terps’ 30-yard field goal with 32 seconds left on the clock sealed the Maryland win. 
 No. 13 Wake Forest stomped out SMU 49-7 with over 500 yards of Demon Deacon offense.
 No. 3 Alabama leads Vanderbilt 21-6 with five minutes to go in the fourth quarter.
 As the afternoon window gets going, we'll be here to keep you updated on everything you need to know. 
 No. 8 Tennessee at Texas A&M as well as No. 9 Indiana versus No. 18 Southern Cal are underway, with No. 1 Georgia versus No. 22 Missouri slated to begin shortly.
 share with Facebook copy link 7:44 pm, November 14, 2026 AP delays Top 25 poll until Monday
 The AP has delayed their weekly Top 25 football poll release by one day after the FAA issued a nationwide groundstop on Nov. 13. The poll, which is usually announced on Sundays, will now be released at 2 p.m. ET on Monday.
 The flight stoppage ultimately altered multiple game times and even pushed No. 19 Ole Miss at Oklahoma to Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET.
 The last time the AP poll release date was delayed was in 2016 following Hurricane Matthew which postponed the Georgia vs. South Carolina game.
 GAME UPDATE: The @OleMissFB at @OU_Football game has been moved to Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 PM ET / Noon CT due to travel issues related to Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stoppage. Television network is TBA. #SECFB
— Southeastern Conference (@SEC) November 14, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 7:31 pm, November 14, 2026 Yankee Stadium hosts decades-old DIII rivalry
 You’ve probably got eyes on Miami, Ohio State or Alabama, but check this out: a DIII football game in Yankee Stadium.
 SUNY Cortland and Ithaca College are playing for the 67th Cortaca Jug today, with the undefeated Red Dragons leading 23-13 approaching the half.
 The stage is set for the 67th annual Cortaca Jug game between @CortlandFB & @IthacaBomberFB on Saturday, November 14, at 1 p.m. ET 🏈 🏟️🎟️ https://t.co/GnnlKkoqGU https://t.co/NVNdsfSiTc
— Yankee Stadium (@yankeestadium) November 12, 2026 
 The two schools, located just over 20 miles apart along Route 13 in upstate New York, have been rivals since the 1930s, playing in what is called “the biggest little game in the nation.”
 The “jug” was introduced in 1959 after Cortland’s Tom Decker and Ithaca’s Dick Carmean decided to etch a trophy into the rivalry’s tradition. 
 Decker bought a $2 ceramic milk jug at a yard sale and the two painted it in their respective school colors, with Cortland winning the inaugural Jug game on Oct. 17, 1959, defeating Ithaca 13–7.
 MURRAY FROM REED AGAIN FOR 6 #OneBeat I #GoBombers https://t.co/qe2ZR5DfZS
— Ithaca Bomber Football (@IthacaBomberFB) November 14, 2026 
 Since then, there have been three jugs, with the newest being unveiled in 2016, to accommodate room for decades of scores and winners.
 The Jug game is traditionally rotated between each school's campus, but the rivalry has made special appearances in major professional sports stadiums.
 In 2019, the Jug game set the all-time NCAA Division III football attendance record with 45,161 fans in MetLife Stadium, with Ithaca winning 32–20. The rivalry game nearly reached the record again in 2022 at Yankee Stadium, drawing in 40,232 fans.
 The Bombers lead the all-time series 42-34-3.

 share with Facebook copy link 4:31 pm, November 14, 2026 What we're watching this week 
 We're in the second week with College Football Playoff rankings — and it's another week of a handful of ranked vs. ranked games that will shake up the top 25.
 More top-10 shakeups ahead? 
 Last week's results meant a new No. 1 (Georgia), a two-loss team now at No. 3 (Alabama), Notre Dame jumping six spots into the top 5 and SEVEN three-loss teams finding a spot in the CFP rankings.
 This week, No. 7 Miami must regroup after dropping from the top spot against Duke, last year's ACC champ. No. 8 Tennessee is thinking SEC title appearance, but the Vols have to travel to Texas A&M. Meanwhile, top-ranked Georgia gets a test from No. 22 Missouri in its first game back at the top. No. 9 Indiana fell five spots on a bye week — and now has to play No. 18 USC.
 Finally, two top-10 teams get major road tests against ranked foes. No. 6 Texas must deal with a likely desperate No. 21 LSU in Death Valley and unbeaten No. 2 Utah travels to face Noah Fifita and No. 23 Arizona in a game moved to 10:30 p.m. because the FAA flight disruptions on Friday.
 CFP ramifications 
 Earlier this week, the CFP announced the playoff field will expand to 24 beginning next season. So this means this season is the last time we'll get a 12-team bracket.
 As a reminder, the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC champs will all receive automatic bids. The highest-ranked team (doesn't need to be a conference champion) from the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12 and Sun Belt will also get in automatically. Right now, that team is No. 24 Boise State , which is serving as the host of ESPN's "College GameDay" today. It's the first time the Broncos have hosted the show since 2010 — also against Oregon State. This year's game will feature the nation's leading rusher (Boise State's Dylan Riley has 1,241 yards) and receiver (Oregon State's Jesse Legree with 1,209 yards). Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson, the top passer in the nation, is out due to injury.
 Record watch 
 Though most eyes will be centered on FBS and the CFP picture, it could be a record-breaking day in DII. Ferris State, which has won four of the last five DII national championships, would break the DII record for consecutive wins if the Bulldogs top Roosevelt today. That would be the 41st win in a row. Last week, Ferris State tied the mark of 40 from Grand Valley State from 2005-07. 
 share with Facebook copy link 4:03 pm, November 14, 2026 UCLA still perfect, Colorado upsets Houston on Friday
 Two ranked teams have already played this week, with No. 4 UCLA and No. 14 Houston both taking the field Friday night.
 No. 4 UCLA 22 , Illinois 14 
 Bruins QB Ty Dieffenbach left the game with a shoulder injury before returning to help his team remain undefeated. UCLA is now 10-0 overall and 7-0 in the Big Ten for the program's best start to a season since 1998.
 Dieffenbach finished with 232 yards and a pair of passing touchdowns. The UCLA defense held the Illini to 240 yards and intercepted three passes.
 Colorado 42 , No. 14 Houston 32 
 The Buffaloes picked up their first win against a top-15 team since 2007 (Oklahoma), rebounding from a 20-7 deficit to get the upset.
 Colorado rushed for 249 yards — the most in the Deion Sanders era — led by Richard Young's 99 yards and two scores. The Buffs had five rushing touchdowns.
